## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Tindukadāyakattheraapadāna* is a verse narrative preserved in the *Therāpadāna* section of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya, designated as Tha Ap 199 [SuttaCentral]. It forms part of the late canonical biographical literature detailing the past deeds and previous rebirths of Buddhist elders. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the text across five languages [SuttaCentral]. No dedicated discussions or citations of this particular text were identified in the sampled secondary literature corpus.
SuttaCentral records no curated cross-language parallels for the text [SuttaCentral], and automated DharmaNexus matching identifies no Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan alignments reaching a score threshold of 10 [DharmaNexus]. However, automated analysis detects substantial Pali-internal text reuse, with 67 matching passages distributed across 18 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest reuse partner is the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (Paṭhamo bhāgo), which accounts for 27 matches and 1,949 shared characters, including an alignment between segments 5.1–6.4 of this apadāna and commentary segments 1353–1357 [DharmaNexus]. The poem also shares extended formulaic segments—predominantly spanning verses 5 to 9—with numerous other apadānas featuring gift-offerings, notably *Phaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 284), *Khajjakadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 165), *Koraṇḍapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 210), *Tiṇasanthārakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 194), *Tiṇasūlakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 159), and the thematic counterpart *Tindukaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 351) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
